steps.body: Length wears many words: a snake is LONG, a tower TALL, a pencil stub SHORT. All describe one attribute — distance end to end.
steps.narration: Length wears many words: a snake is LONG, a tower TALL, a pencil stub SHORT. All describe one attribute — distance end to end.

widget.prompt: Measure the scarf. Align zero with its start, then place 5 one-unit blocks with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: 5 equal blocks cover the scarf exactly — same start, no gaps, no overlaps: that number IS its length.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: A tower tips onto its side. Its TALL becomes…
predict.reveal: Length survives turning; only the word changes with the pose.

cml.actionGoal: Compare fairly — same start line, level seesaw, one sorting rule — for kmd length words.
invariants: Fair comparison has fixed rules: lengths compare from one same start line, weights compare by which pan sinks, and sorted groups compare by their counts — the anchors for kmd length words.
misconceptions: Judging length before aligning starts, reading size as weight, or comparing groups by how much space they fill instead of their counts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the starts were not lined up, could the far ends still settle which is longer?

widget.prompt: A tower is TALL and a snake is LONG. What do the two words share?

options.label: Both describe length
options.feedback: Correct — tall is length measured upward; long is length measured along; same attribute, two poses.

options.label: Nothing — they are unrelated
options.feedback: Turn the tower on its side and tall becomes long; one attribute wears both words.

options.label: Tall means heavy
options.feedback: Tall speaks of height, not weight — a tall tower of feathers stays light.

options.label: Long means old
options.feedback: Long measures distance end to end, whatever the age of the snake.

widget.prompt: Compare the three ribbons from one start line and tap the longest.

items.label: top ribbon
items.feedback: The top one measures 4 cubes — shorter than 6. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

items.label: bottom ribbon
items.feedback: The bottom one measures 2 cubes — shorter than 6. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

widget.missFeedback: From one start line the far end decides: the longest reaches 6 cubes.
widget.successFeedback: Right — same start line, so the farther end IS the longest.
